source: Keepa product record as the owner's app stored it (cache/keepa), slimmed to the identity fields; and what the app did with it (scan/matches.json, scan/prices.json, scan/partPrices.json)
what: Amazon's own catalog record carries the wrong part number. The listing is a DWST60122-1 backpack; its partNumber and model fields say DWST08017 (a TOUGHSYSTEM adaptor plate, $39.99 at Home Depot). The catalog rule confirmed it for DWST08017 and switched to it from another listing; the set 'Adaptor Plate for TOUGHSYSTEM 2.0 and 10-Compartment Shallow Pro Small Parts Organizer' ($54.87) then read +$259.45, ROI 473%. The owner caught it by eye. The title check missed it because the DEWALT model pattern knows only DC… models.
